title: Dog Day Afternoon review
transcript:
I've never seen the movie Dog Day Afternoon
so I went into this play completely blind,
other than knowing it was about a bank robbery.
I had assumed the robbery was just the inciting incident,
but let's just say it lasted way longer than I expected it to.
As it evolves into an hours-long hostage situation
and a stand off with the police,
the burglars and hostages end up getting cozy with one another
and finding their shared humanity.
I was at the second preview and I thought it was already in pretty good shape.
The script by Pulitzer winner Stephen Adly Guirgis is solid and feels suited to the time,
and the performances are strong,
with Jessica Hecht being the standout.
I find it interesting that Jon Bernthal
and Ebon Moss-Bachrach are both listed above the title
when Jon's role as Sonny is so much bigger.
That said, I was more impressed by Ebon’s heartbreaking portrayal of Sal,
and I felt like he was totally underused.
There are a couple of tone and pacing things
that are probably still being calibrated,
but the comedy was enjoyable even when the tension was lacking.
And while the momentum isn't always there,
it's a rolling boil when it is.
I appreciated the gloriously sprawling bank set
which almost justifies putting this show in such a big theatre,
but I still felt very far away being in the mid-mezz for a play like this.
Regardless, I ended up really enjoying this show —
it had to grow on me, but I can see why
the film is a classic, being a comedy thriller with anti-establishment messaging.
Again, I haven't actually seen the film,
so I can't speak to how faithful this adaptation is.
For all I know, this version completely butchers it.
But in strictly theatrical terms,
I could have believed that this wasn't even based on a film,
and I think that's a good thing.
With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly enjoyed the show despite some reservations about pacing and tone. They explicitly state 'I ended up really enjoying this show' and praise multiple elements including the script, performances, and set design.
